 SCCH-24 3 MVC No.1846/2024  JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 13-07-2023 at about 7-30 pm., the petitioner was riding the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-JC-7729 along with his son by name Punitha Sai as a pillion ride on Y N Hosakote-Doddahalli road and when they reached near Govt Hospital, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EQ-7863 came from Doddahalli towards Y N Hosakote in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner and his son fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Y N Hosakote, Pavagada, Tumkur and then he was shifted to K N Hospital Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient.
So far, the petitioner has spent sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards medicine, treatment etc.,
The doctor has advised him to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant from the fracture site.

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 36 years.
He was working as Laborer under private and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

4. The Respondent no.1 /the Insurer of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EQ-7863 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.1 has contended that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license and that the concerned police authority has filed the case u/Sec. 279, 337, 338 of IPC r/w Section 181, 180 of MV Act and that the respondent no.2 and 3 being the owner as on the date of accident has contravened the provisions of MV Act and that the claim petition is barred by limitation.

The respondent no.1 further contended that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident, the petitioner in collision with the jurisdiction police has created false crime records about the manner and involvement of motorcycle to get compensation and that there is delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint.

It is further contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself and that there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the insured vehicle.

Hence, submitted to dismiss the petition against the respondent no.1.
5.
On service of notice, the Respondent no.2 did not appear before the tribunal, hence he was placed ex- parte.
6. In response to the summons, though the Respondent No.3 has appeared through his counsel but did not contest the case.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident on 13-07-2023 at about 7-30 pm., Infront Govt Hospital, Y N Hosakote-Doddahalli road, Pavagada Taluk, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EQ-7863 ?

10. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

REASONS 11. Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 13-07-2023 at about 7-30 pm., the petitioner was riding the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JC-7729 along with his son by name Punitha Sai as a pillion ride on Y N Hosakote- Doddahalli road and when they reached near Govt Hospital, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-16-EQ-7863 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came from Doddahalli towards Y N Hosakote in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner and his son fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
12.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 12 which are the police records such as F.I.R, complaint, Spot mahazar, spot photographs,
wound certificate, notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act, reply to the notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act, IMV report,
Indemnity bond, photographs of the offending vehicles, charge sheet, statement of witnesses, etc.,
13.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Nagaraja C , case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.0059/2023 by Y N Hosakote Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section under section 279 and 279, 337, 338 of IPC and u/Sec. 181,180 of MV Act.
14.

The learned counsel for respondent no.1 who is the contesting respondent has vehemently argued that as on the date of the accident the petitioner was not holding valid driving license and that the motor cycle of the petitioner had no Insurance Policy, hence the petitioner too has contributed negligence.

The learned counsel in further has argued that the spot of the accident is in the middle of the road and the petitioner even having seen the offending vehicle at a distance of 100 meter, not tried to avoid the accident.
Hence the petitioner has also contributed negligence.
The learned counsel in further has submitted about the delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint.

15. If the materials placed on record is perused, the accident in question has occurred on 13.07.2023 and complaint came to be lodged on 20.07.2023 and there is delay of 7 days in lodging the Sharan Kumar C N vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61614441/

sentences.text: The complainant is none other than the father of the petitioner who admittedly is not an eye witness to the accident.
In the complaint and in the FIR reason for delay has been explained stating that the complaint was engaged in providing treatment to the petitioner.

If discharge summary issued from Kannva Hospital is perused wherein there is reference about the treatment take by the petitioner on 13.07.2023 at Nimhans hospital and KG Hospital and thereafter he came to Kannva hospital for treatment.

In the MLC Register produced by the petitioner at Ex.P20 there is mention about involvement of two wheeler in the accident and the history of injury is mentioned as RTA hit between two wheeler and two wheeler.

From the aforesaid materials it can be gathered that though complaint was lodged after 7 days of the accident but soon after the accident the petitioner had taken treatment on the history of injury sustained in the road traffic accident.
Hence the delay has been properly explained.

16. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, it is not in dispute that on the date of accident, the petitioner was proceeding from Y.N.Hosakote towards Doddahalli and offending vehicle came from opposite direction i.e., from Doddahalli towards Y.N.Hosakote hit to the motor cycle of the petitioner.

If the spot mahazar is perused, the width of the road at the spot of the accident is nearly 12 feet and the accident in question has occurred not on the middle of the road as submitted by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 but on the extreme northern side of the road.

When the offending vehicle was proceeding from Doddahalli towards Y.N.Hosakote he ought to have drive his vehicle on the left side of his road but by driving the vehicle on the extreme right side of his road hit to the motor cycle of the petitioner.
Had the rider of the offending vehicle drive his vehicle on the left side of his road this accident would not have occurred.

Though the learned counsel for respondent no.1 has argued that due to the rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle by the petitioner is the cause for accident but they have failed to examine the driver/rider of the offending vehicle.
Even respondent no.3 who is the owner of the offending vehicle has failed to rebut the evidence given by the petitioner by examining the rider of the offending vehicle.
Respondent no.2 is the policy holder of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident and respondent no.3 is the RC owner of the said vehicle.
They have uncontested the case.
It is true that the official of respondent no.1 company is examined as RW.1 but they are not the competent witness to speak about the manner of the accident.
Hence the evidence of PW.1 coupled with police records which clearly proves the sole negligence contributed by the rider of the offending vehicle.
17. So far as not holding driving license by the petitioner and not having insurance policy in respect of the vehicle of the petitioner is concerned, the PW.1 has admitted the said fact.

But in a Judgment rendered by the Hon'ble High Court, Kulburgi Bench in MFA NO.202104/2024 between the Branch Manager ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Vs Pooja and others rendered on 19.09.2024,
it was observed that, "if a person drives a vehicle without a license, he commits an offence.

sentences.text: The same, by itself, in our opinion, may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.
It has been held by the courts below that it was the driver of the mini truck who was driving rashly and negligently.
It is one thing to say that the appellant was not possessing any license but no finding of fact has been arrived at that he was driving the two wheeler rashly and negligently.

If he was not driving rashly and negligently which contributed to the accident, we fail to see as to how, only because he was not having a license, he would be held to be guilty of contributory negligence".

19. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summaries which are marked at Ex.P5 and P13.

On going through the medical documents it reveal that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at District Hospital, Tumakur from 13-07-2023 to 14-07-2023 and then shifted to Kannva Sri Sai Hospital from 14-07- 2023 to 20-07-2023 wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 8 days.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained three injuries which are grievous in nature.

20. Manith Kumar H -MRO at Kannva Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW.2 and through him MLC register, Police Intimation, case sheet are marked as Ex.P20 to Ex.P22.
21.
Dr. N Chaitanya Babu.
- Dental Surgeon, clinic at Basaveshwarnagar, Bangalore is examined as PW.3 and through him OPD slip and x-ray are marked as Ex.P23 and Ex.P24.
P.W.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 30-06-2025 for assessment of disability of orofacial injury.
The PW.3 further deposed that fracture of right zygomatic bone of maxilla and nasal bone fracture at 20%.
Total 20% resultant disability of petitioner is 20% in respect to whole body and that the petitioner sustained permanent disability in respect to his maxilla (upper jaw) and nasal Bone.

22. PW.3 further deposed that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of screws and plates,
the estimated cost of this surgery would be around Rs.1,00,000/-.
23.
If the cross examination of PW.3 is perused, admittedly he is not a treated doctor.
It is admitted by PW.3 that as the day rolls on, there is possibility of improving the health condition of the petitioner.
Admittedly PW.3 has not given estimation for the future medical expenses.

If the evidence of PW.3 is carefully perused, in the evidence in chief the PW.3 has deposed that the petitioner will be able to look normal i.e., aesthetic function will become normal but the ability to bite hard food will be restricted to 50% only.
According to the PW.3 the petitioner has sustained permanent disability in respect to his maxilla and nasal bone.
Considering the evidence of PW.3 it can be said that the PW.3 has assessed the disability on higher side.
Further even if there is any disability suffered by the petitioner it would not come in the way of discharging his work so as to effect his future income.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future loss of income.
Further there is no reason to believe that for removal of implant the petitioner may have incurred expenses to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.50,000/-.
24. Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
25. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained three grievous injuries .

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for Sharan Kumar C N vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61614441/

sentences.text: treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs 70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
26. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 35 medical bills for Rs.2,62,507/- as per Ex.P15.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,62,507/- under the head medical expenses.
27. It is stated that petitioner was working as a mason under private building contractor and was earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, he has not produced any document to prove his income and avocation.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence considers the income of the petitioner as Rs. 16,000/- p.m.
28.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 8 days as an inpatient in Kannva Sri Sai Hospital.
Hence, it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period.

Hence, taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this Tribunal takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,000/- p.m for two months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.32,000/-
towards loss of income during the laid down period.
29. From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Kannva Sri Sai Hospital.
For 08 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs 20,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2023.

30. The petitioner at his age of 36 years has sustained grievous injuries to his Maxilla (Upper jaw)
which definitely would cause some amount of loss of amenities, discomfort and facial disfiguration in life.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities,
discomforts and facial disfiguration to the tune of Rs.1,50,000/-.

sentences.text: Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,84,507/- (Rupees Five Lakh Eighty Four Thousand Five Hundred Seven only).
31. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.

32. The learned counsel for respondent no.1 has submitted that as on the date of accident the rider of the offending vehicle had no driving license and the respondent no3 who is the owner of the said vehicle had permitted the accused to ride the said vehicle having knowledge that the accused had no driving license, hence there is fundamental breach of contract, hence submitted to exonerate the Insurance Company from the liability of paying compensation and to fix the liability on the respondent no.3.
33.

If the charge sheet is perused, the charge sheet was filed against the rider of offending vehicle even for the offence u/Sec.3(1), 181 181 of MV Act alleging that at the time of accident the rider was not holding valid driving license.

34. The petitioner has seriously refuted the said contention taken by the respondent no.1 and submitted that, as on the date of accident the rider was holding valid driving license to ride the motorcycle and respondent no.1 in order to escape from the liability now contending that the rider was not holding valid driving license and that the respondent no.1 has not issued notice to the owner/respondent no.3 to produce the driving license of the rider of the offending vehicle and they have not examined the RTO to prove that the rider was not holding valid driving license, hence merely on the bald statement of the respondent no.1 it cannot be concluded that rider was not holding valid driving license.

It is further submitted that even if for any reason this court comes to the conclusion that the rider was not holding valid driving license then also at the first instance the respondent no.1 has to pay the compensation and to recover the amount from the respondent no.3 under pay and recovery.

35. In order to prove that the rider was not holding valid driving license, the respondent no.1 has relied upon the notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given thereto, charge sheet etc.,
36.

It is true that respondent no.1 has not issued notice to the respondent no.3 to produce the driving license of the rider of offending vehicle and they have not examined the RTO to prove that as on the date of accident the rider was not holding valid driving license but if the reply to the notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act is perused, the respondent no.3 being the owner has not furnished the particulars of the Driving license and admitted that as on the date of the accident the rider was not holding Driving license.
Further respondent no.3 on service of summons from the court though has appeared before the court but uncontested the case.
If really the rider of the offending vehicle had driving license then nothing prevented the respondent no.3 from producing the driving license of the rider of the motorcycle.
Further admittedly charge sheet was filed against the rider of the motorcycle even for offence u/Sec. 181 of IMV Act.

Hence, from the materials placed on record it can be said that as on the date of accident the rider was not holding valid driving license.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent no.1 has submitted that subsequent to the amendment no pay and recovery can be ordered.

It is submitted by the learned counsel that, the right to recover compensation from the owner of the offending vehicle flows from the proviso attached to sub section (4) of section 149 of M.V. Act 1988 has been omitted by Act of 2019 and therefore in case of a breach of policy, it is only the owner against whom award can be directly made and insurer is liable to be relieved from any liability to indemnify the owner.
38.

Per contra the learned counsel for petitioner has submitted that even though accident in question has occurred subsequent to the amendment to MV Act but pay and recovery still be ordered against the Insurance Company.

39. The Learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the order passed in First Appeal No.
1776/2024 between ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co.Ltd., VS. Smt. Arti Devi & 4 Ors., wherein it was observed that "mere omission of proviso attached to sub-section (4) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 after its replacement by Section 150 of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (32 of 2019), neither takes away the liability of the insurer to pay the claimants nor its right to recover the said amount from the owner.

Principle of law laid down by the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swaran Singh and others, JT 2004 (1) SC 109 has not lost its significance and binding effect despite omission of proviso".

sentences.text: In the said case also the accident in question was occurred subsequent to the amendment i.e., on 21-08- 2022 and in the said case also the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving license to drive the vehicle.

The Hon'ble High Court in the given set of fact has observed that even though there is violation of policy condition by the owner of the lorry but as MV Act is a benevolent legislation, the claimants cannot be deprived of the compensation so awarded.

Therefore, the Hon'ble High Court has directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation, as the policy was in force as on the date of accident and Insurance company has to indemnify the said compensation so awarded and to recover the same from the owner of the lorry by executing the award against to him.
43. Further in Civil Appeal No.1175/2025 (arising out of SLP (C) No.377/2023) between M.Ananthi and Others Vs P. Venkatesan and Another.

entities.text: M.Ananthi and Others Vs P. Venkatesan and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case also the driver of the offending vehicle had no driving license.
The tribunal and Hon'ble High Court has absolved the Insurance Company from the liability of paying the compensation.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that " In so far as the liability on the Insurance Company is concerned, the courts below have rightly held that since the driver of the offending vehicle was not having any license to drive the same, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to compensate".
But further observed that while granting the compensation the tribunal High Court ought to have directed the Insurance Company to pay the sum and recover the same from the owner.

The Hon'ble Supreme court in the said case has referred the Judgment rendered in National Insurance Company Ltd Vs Swaran Singh and others (2004)3 SCC 297, wherein it was held that "the claimant should not be allowed to suffer and run about to release the compensation awarded and that, it is in the fitness of things that the Insurance Company in such cases should first pay and then recover the amount".

sentences.text: In the present case it is proved by the respondent no.1 that as on the date of accident, the rider had no valid driving license to ride the vehicle and thereby there is breach of policy condition.

But by relying upon the observation made in the aforesaid judgments, this court orders the insurance company to pay the compensation amount and then to recover the amount from the owner under the principle of pay and recovery.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioners along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount and to recover the said amount from the Respondent no.3.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
47. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER  The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,84,507/- (Rupees Five Lakh Eighty Four Thousand Five Hundred Seven only) with interest at 6% per annum on sum of Rs.5,34,507/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award and to recover the said amount from the respondent no.3/owner of the offending vehicle.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

from whom?

opennyai_summary.arguments:
If the charge sheet is perused, the charge sheet was filed against the rider of offending vehicle even for the offence u/Sec.3(1), 181 181 of MV Act alleging that at the time of accident the rider was not holding valid driving license.
It is true that respondent no.1 has not issued notice to the respondent no.3 to produce the driving license of the rider of offending vehicle and they have not examined the RTO to prove that as on the date of accident the rider was not holding valid driving license but if the reply to the notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act is perused, the respondent no.3 being the owner has not furnished the particulars of the Driving license and admitted that as on the date of the accident the rider was not holding Driving license.
If really the rider of the offending vehicle had driving license then nothing prevented the respondent no.3 from producing the driving license of the rider of the motorcycle.
Hence, from the materials placed on record it can be said that as on the date of accident the rider was not holding valid driving license.
